svg.text: What a screening rule buys an allocator
Rank the cohort by one field available the week of publication, fund the top slice, and count the eventually-adopted
share of the papers that get adopted, captured
Cohort: 6,134 papers published 2023-06 to 2025-03, of which 73 are named by a top-1,000 model. Every paper has had 18+ months of exposure.
At a half budget upvotes has caught 97% and stars 61% — 43% of this cohort has no repo, so the star rule cannot rank them at all.
This does NOT contradict 1-no-predictor. No rule picks a winner; a rule still shrinks the field 5.6-fold at this budget. Picking and portfolio are different questions.
The outcome counted here is 'named by any top-1,000 model', which is overwhelmingly a lab citing itself — see 8-two-positives.
